name: Wadiyari
catalog_citation: Zubair, Saeed. 2016. A Phonological Description of Wadiyari, a Language Spoken in Pakistan. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. PDF: https://www.ialtrust.org/resources/A-Phonological-Description-of-Wadiyari.pdf (187 pp.)
catalog_locator: sec. 4.6 'Stress', pp. 89-94 (rule p.89-90, tetrasyllabic note p.93-94, summary p.94); also sec. 4.7/ch.5 summary p.98-99
catalog_quote: Stress in the Wadiyari language is realized as a higher pitch on the stressed syllable. The stress is predictable and the primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word if the final syllable is light (without coda or diphthong). However, when the final syllable is heavy, (i.e., a closed syllable word or if the final syllable has a diphthong) the primary stress is placed on the final syllable of the word. Some examples are as follows: Open and light syllable words: #1015 /ˈtʰa.pa/ ‘footprint’ #954 /ʈə.ˈko.ɾi/ ‘bell’ #700 /ʃe.wa.ˈda.ɾi/ ‘host’ Open and heavy syllable words: #137 /zə.ˈɭoi/ ‘water leech’ #371 /ɓəd.ˈdai/ ‘all’ Closed (heavy) syllable words: #1204 /po.ˈpəʈ/ ‘parrot’ #85 /zə.na.ˈwəɾ/ ‘animal’ ... The language has tetrasyllabic words with heavy syllables - such as /bad.ˈla.w /, and /kʰan.kə.ˈzu.ɾo/, and so on, which need some explanation as to why they are not str…
